paper_title: Quantum Mechanics of Stochastic Systems (Kuang, 2025, arXiv)
core_reasoning_1:
\subsection*{Claim}
For a stochastic state
\[
|\psi_S\rangle=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\alpha^{(S)}_n |n\rangle,
\qquad |\alpha^{(S)}_n|^2=P_S(n),
\]
in an orthonormal number basis satisfying \(\hat N|n\rangle=n|n\rangle\), if \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P_S(n)=1\), then \(|\psi_S\rangle\) is normalized and, for every integer \(q\geq 1\) for which the series converges,
\[
\langle \psi_S|\hat N^q|\psi_S\rangle=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n^qP_S(n).
\]

\subsection*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \langle n|m\rangle=\delta_{nm}\quad\text{for all }n,m\in\mathbb{N}_0.\\
\text{(P2)} & \hat N|n\rangle=n|n\rangle\quad\text{for all }n\in\mathbb{N}_0.\\
\text{(P3)} & |\psi_S\rangle:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\alpha^{(S)}_n|n\rangle.\\
\text{(P4)} & P_S(n):=|\alpha^{(S)}_n|^2.\\
\text{(P5)} & \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P_S(n)=1.\\
\text{(P6)} & q\in\mathbb{N}\text{ and }\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n^qP_S(n)<\infty.\\
\text{(P7)} & \hat N^q|n\rangle=n^q|n\rangle\quad\text{follows by repeated application of (P2).}
\end{array}
\]

\subsection*{Derivation}
\begin{align}
\langle \psi_S|\psi_S\rangle
&=\left(\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}(\alpha^{(S)}_m)^*\langle m|\right)
  \left(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\alpha^{(S)}_n|n\rangle\right)
  &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(\alpha^{(S)}_m)^*\alpha^{(S)}_n\langle m|n\rangle
  &&\text{bilinearity}\\
&=\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(\alpha^{(S)}_m)^*\alpha^{(S)}_n\delta_{mn}
  &&\text{by (P1)}\\
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}|\alpha^{(S)}_n|^2
  &&\text{Kronecker-delta reduction}\\
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P_S(n)
  &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=1
  &&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
For the count-operator moment,
\begin{align}
\langle \psi_S|\hat N^q|\psi_S\rangle
&=\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(\alpha^{(S)}_m)^*\alpha^{(S)}_n\langle m|\hat N^q|n\rangle
  &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(\alpha^{(S)}_m)^*\alpha^{(S)}_n n^q\langle m|n\rangle
  &&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(\alpha^{(S)}_m)^*\alpha^{(S)}_n n^q\delta_{mn}
  &&\text{by (P1)}\\
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n^q|\alpha^{(S)}_n|^2
  &&\text{Kronecker-delta reduction}\\
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n^qP_S(n)
  &&\text{by (P4) and (P6)}.
\end{align}

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\langle \psi_S|\psi_S\rangle=1\quad\text{and}\quad
\langle \psi_S|\hat N^q|\psi_S\rangle=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n^qP_S(n)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_3:
\subsection*{Claim}
If
\[
\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}=\hbar\omega\left(\hat a^\dagger\hat a+\frac{1}{2}\right),
\qquad
\Delta V_{\mathrm{Pois}}:=\hbar\omega\left(-\alpha\hat a^\dagger-\alpha^*\hat a+|\alpha|^2\right),
\]
and \(\hat H_{\mathrm{Pois}}:=\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}+\Delta V_{\mathrm{Pois}}\), then the coherent state \(|\alpha\rangle=\hat D(\alpha)|0\rangle\) is an eigenstate of \(\hat H_{\mathrm{Pois}}\) with eigenvalue \(\hbar\omega/2\).

\subsection*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}:=\hbar\omega\left(\hat a^\dagger\hat a+\dfrac{1}{2}\right).\\
\text{(P2)} & \hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}|0\rangle=\dfrac{1}{2}\hbar\omega|0\rangle.\\
\text{(P3)} & |\alpha\rangle:=\hat D(\alpha)|0\rangle.\\
\text{(P4)} & \hat D(\alpha)\hat a\hat D^\dagger(\alpha)=\hat a-\alpha.\\
\text{(P5)} & \hat D(\alpha)\hat a^\dagger\hat D^\dagger(\alpha)=\hat a^\dagger-\alpha^*.\\
\text{(P6)} & \hat D^\dagger(\alpha)\hat D(\alpha)=I.\\
\text{(P7)} & \Delta V_{\mathrm{Pois}}:=\hbar\omega\left(-\alpha\hat a^\dagger-\alpha^*\hat a+|\alpha|^2\right).\\
\text{(P8)} & \hat H_{\mathrm{Pois}}:=\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}+\Delta V_{\mathrm{Pois}}.
\end{array}
\]

\subsection*{Derivation}
\begin{align}
\hat D(\alpha)\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}\hat D^\dagger(\alpha)
&=\hbar\omega\left(\hat D(\alpha)\hat a^\dagger\hat D^\dagger(\alpha)\hat D(\alpha)\hat a\hat D^\dagger(\alpha)+\frac{1}{2}\right)
  &&\text{by (P1) and (P6)}\\
&=\hbar\omega\left((\hat a^\dagger-\alpha^*)(\hat a-\alpha)+\frac{1}{2}\right)
  &&\text{by (P4) and (P5)}\\
&=\hbar\omega\left(\hat a^\dagger\hat a-\alpha\hat a^\dagger-\alpha^*\hat a+|\alpha|^2+\frac{1}{2}\right)
  &&\text{expansion}\\
&=\hbar\omega\left(\hat a^\dagger\hat a+\frac{1}{2}\right)
  +\hbar\omega\left(-\alpha\hat a^\dagger-\alpha^*\hat a+|\alpha|^2\right)
  &&\text{regrouping}\\
&=\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}+\Delta V_{\mathrm{Pois}}
  &&\text{by (P1) and (P7)}\\
&=\hat H_{\mathrm{Pois}}
  &&\text{by (P8)}.
\end{align}
Thus,
\begin{align}
\hat H_{\mathrm{Pois}}|\alpha\rangle
&=\hat D(\alpha)\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}\hat D^\dagger(\alpha)\hat D(\alpha)|0\rangle
  &&\text{by the identity above and (P3)}\\
&=\hat D(\alpha)\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}|0\rangle
  &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\hat D(\alpha)\left(\frac{1}{2}\hbar\omega|0\rangle\right)
  &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\hbar\omega\hat D(\alpha)|0\rangle
  &&\text{linearity}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\hbar\omega|\alpha\rangle
  &&\text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\hat H_{\mathrm{Pois}}|\alpha\rangle=\frac{1}{2}\hbar\omega|\alpha\rangle}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_5:
\subsection*{Claim}
For \(0<p<1\), define the zero-based Negative Binomial stochastic amplitudes by
\[
\alpha^{(NB)}_n(r,p):=\sqrt{\binom{n+r-1}{n}(1-p)^r p^n},\qquad n\in\mathbb{N}_0,
\]
and define the zero-based Geometric amplitudes by
\[
\alpha^{(G)}_n(p):=\sqrt{(1-p)p^n},\qquad n\in\mathbb{N}_0.
\]
Then the Geometric stochastic state is exactly the \(r=1\) member of the Negative Binomial family. Equivalently, if a one-based Geometric waiting-time amplitude is written with success parameter \(q\) as
\[
\widetilde{\alpha}^{(G)}_k(q):=\sqrt{q(1-q)^{k-1}},\qquad k\in\mathbb{N},
\]
then the two conventions agree under \(q:=1-p\) and \(k:=n+1\).

\subsection*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & 0<p<1,\quad r\in\mathbb{N},\quad n\in\mathbb{N}_0.\\
\text{(P2)} & \alpha^{(NB)}_n(r,p):=\sqrt{\binom{n+r-1}{n}(1-p)^rp^n}.\\
\text{(P3)} & |\psi_{NB}(r,p)\rangle:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\alpha^{(NB)}_n(r,p)|n\rangle.\\
\text{(P4)} & \alpha^{(G)}_n(p):=\sqrt{(1-p)p^n}.\\
\text{(P5)} & |\psi_G(p)\rangle:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\alpha^{(G)}_n(p)|n\rangle.\\
\text{(P6)} & \widetilde{\alpha}^{(G)}_k(q):=\sqrt{q(1-q)^{k-1}},\quad k\in\mathbb{N},\quad 0<q<1.\\
\text{(P7)} & \binom{n}{n}=1\quad\text{for all }n\in\mathbb{N}_0.\\
\text{(P8)} & q:=1-p,\quad k:=n+1.
\end{array}
\]

\subsection*{Derivation}
First substitute \(r=1\) into the zero-based Negative Binomial amplitude:
\begin{align}
\alpha^{(NB)}_n(1,p)
&=\sqrt{\binom{n+1-1}{n}(1-p)^1p^n}
  &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\sqrt{\binom{n}{n}(1-p)p^n}
  &&\text{arithmetic in the binomial coefficient}\\
&=\sqrt{(1-p)p^n}
  &&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=\alpha^{(G)}_n(p)
  &&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align}
Thus the corresponding state vectors have identical coefficients in the same orthonormal number basis:
\begin{align}
|\psi_{NB}(1,p)\rangle
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\alpha^{(NB)}_n(1,p)|n\rangle
  &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\alpha^{(G)}_n(p)|n\rangle
  &&\text{coefficient equality above}\\
&=|\psi_G(p)\rangle
  &&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
For the one-based waiting-time convention, substitute \(q:=1-p\) and \(k:=n+1\):
\begin{align}
\widetilde{\alpha}^{(G)}_{n+1}(1-p)
&=\sqrt{(1-p)\bigl(1-(1-p)\bigr)^{(n+1)-1}}
  &&\text{by (P6) and (P8)}\\
&=\sqrt{(1-p)p^n}
  &&\text{algebra}\\
&=\alpha^{(NB)}_n(1,p)
  &&\text{by the first coefficient identity}.
\end{align}

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{|\psi_G(p)\rangle=|\psi_{NB}(1,p)\rangle\quad\text{and}\quad \widetilde{\alpha}^{(G)}_{n+1}(1-p)=\alpha^{(NB)}_n(1,p)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\subsection*{Claim}
For fixed \(\lambda>0\), define
\[
B_{n,k}:=\binom{n}{k}\left(\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^k\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^{n-k}\quad(0\leq k\leq n),
\qquad
P_k:=e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^k}{k!},
\]
and set \(B_{n,k}:=0\) for \(k>n\). If
\[
|\psi_B(n,\lambda/n)\rangle:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\sqrt{B_{n,k}}|k\rangle,
\qquad
|\psi_P(\lambda)\rangle:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\sqrt{P_k}|k\rangle,
\]
then the Binomial stochastic system converges strongly to the Poisson stochastic system:
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\left\||\psi_B(n,\lambda/n)\rangle-|\psi_P(\lambda)\rangle\right\|=0.
\]

\subsection*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \lambda>0\text{ is fixed, and eventually }n>\lambda.\\
\text{(P2)} & B_{n,k}:=\binom{n}{k}(\lambda/n)^k(1-\lambda/n)^{n-k}\text{ for }0\leq k\leq n,\text{ and }B_{n,k}:=0\text{ for }k>n.\\
\text{(P3)} & P_k:=e^{-\lambda}\lambda^k/k!\quad\text{for }k\in\mathbb{N}_0.\\
\text{(P4)} & |\psi_B(n,\lambda/n)\rangle:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\sqrt{B_{n,k}}|k\rangle,
\quad |\psi_P(\lambda)\rangle:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\sqrt{P_k}|k\rangle.\\
\text{(P5)} & \langle k|\ell\rangle=\delta_{k\ell}\quad\text{for all }k,\ell\in\mathbb{N}_0.\\
\text{(P6)} & \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B_{n,k}=1\quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}P_k=1.\\
\text{(P7)} & \lim_{n\to\infty}(1-\lambda/n)^n=e^{-\lambda}.\\
\text{(P8)} & \text{For fixed }k,\quad \lim_{n\to\infty}\prod_{s=0}^{k-1}\left(1-\frac{s}{n}\right)=1\quad\text{and}\quad \lim_{n\to\infty}(1-\lambda/n)^{-k}=1.\\
\text{(P9)} & 0\leq (\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{y})^2\leq x+y\quad\text{for all }x,y\geq 0.
\end{array}
\]

\subsection*{Derivation}
For any fixed \(k\in\mathbb{N}_0\) and all \(n\geq k\), rewrite the Binomial probability as
\begin{align}
B_{n,k}
&=\binom{n}{k}\left(\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^k\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^{n-k}
  &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\frac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-k+1)}{k!}\frac{\lambda^k}{n^k}\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^n\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^{-k}
  &&\text{expanding }\binom{n}{k}\\
&=\frac{\lambda^k}{k!}\prod_{s=0}^{k-1}\left(1-\frac{s}{n}\right)\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^n\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^{-k}
  &&\text{factoring }n^k.
\end{align}
Taking the limit term by term for fixed \(k\) gives
\begin{align}
\lim_{n\to\infty}B_{n,k}
&=\frac{\lambda^k}{k!}\cdot 1\cdot e^{-\lambda}\cdot 1
  &&\text{by (P7) and (P8)}\\
&=P_k
  &&\text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
Hence, for fixed \(k\),
\begin{align}
\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\sqrt{B_{n,k}}-\sqrt{P_k}\right)^2
&=0
  &&\text{continuity of }x\mapsto\sqrt{x}\text{ on }[0,\infty).
\end{align}
Now define the squared Hilbert-space distance
\begin{align}
d_n^2
&:=\left\||\psi_B(n,\lambda/n)\rangle-|\psi_P(\lambda)\rangle\right\|^2\\
&=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left(\sqrt{B_{n,k}}-\sqrt{P_k}\right)^2
  &&\text{by (P4) and (P5)}.
\end{align}
Let \(\varepsilon>0\). Since \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}P_k=1\), choose \(K\) such that
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=K+1}^{\infty}P_k&<\varepsilon
  &&\text{by (P6)}.
\end{align}
For this fixed \(K\), pointwise convergence on the finite set \(\{0,\ldots,K\}\) implies that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=0}^{K}\left(\sqrt{B_{n,k}}-\sqrt{P_k}\right)^2&<\varepsilon,\\
\sum_{k=0}^{K}B_{n,k}&>\sum_{k=0}^{K}P_k-\varepsilon.
\end{align}
Using normalization, the Binomial tail is bounded by
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=K+1}^{\infty}B_{n,k}
&=1-\sum_{k=0}^{K}B_{n,k}
  &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&<1-\sum_{k=0}^{K}P_k+\varepsilon
  &&\text{finite partial-sum bound}\\
&=\sum_{k=K+1}^{\infty}P_k+\varepsilon
  &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&<2\varepsilon
  &&\text{by the choice of }K.
\end{align}
Therefore, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\begin{align}
d_n^2
&=\sum_{k=0}^{K}\left(\sqrt{B_{n,k}}-\sqrt{P_k}\right)^2
 +\sum_{k=K+1}^{\infty}\left(\sqrt{B_{n,k}}-\sqrt{P_k}\right)^2\\
&<\varepsilon+\sum_{k=K+1}^{\infty}(B_{n,k}+P_k)
  &&\text{by (P9)}\\
&<\varepsilon+2\varepsilon+\varepsilon
  &&\text{tail bounds above}\\
&=4\varepsilon.
\end{align}
Since \(\varepsilon>0\) is arbitrary and \(d_n^2\geq 0\), it follows that \(\lim_{n\to\infty}d_n^2=0\), hence \(\lim_{n\to\infty}d_n=0\).

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\lim_{n\to\infty}\left\||\psi_B(n,\lambda/n)\rangle-|\psi_P(\lambda)\rangle\right\|=0}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_8:
\subsection*{Claim}
For the Binomial stochastic amplitude
\[
\alpha^{(B)}_k(p)=\sqrt{\binom{N}{k}p^k(1-p)^{N-k}},
\qquad N\in\mathbb{N},\quad 0<p<1,
\]
the quantum Fisher information with respect to \(p\),
\[
F(\psi_B):=4\sum_{k=0}^{N}\left|\frac{d\alpha^{(B)}_k}{dp}\right|^2,
\]
equals
\[
F(\psi_B)=\frac{N}{p(1-p)}.
\]

\subsection*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & N\in\mathbb{N},\quad 0<p<1,\quad k\in\{0,\ldots,N\}.\\
\text{(P2)} & \alpha^{(B)}_k(p):=\sqrt{\binom{N}{k}p^k(1-p)^{N-k}}.\\
\text{(P3)} & P_B(k,p):=|\alpha^{(B)}_k(p)|^2=\binom{N}{k}p^k(1-p)^{N-k}.\\
\text{(P4)} & F(\psi_B):=4\sum_{k=0}^{N}\left|d\alpha^{(B)}_k/dp\right|^2.\\
\text{(P5)} & \sum_{k=0}^{N}\binom{N}{k}x^k y^{N-k}=(x+y)^N.\\
\text{(P6)} & \dfrac{d}{dp}\log\alpha^{(B)}_k(p)=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{k}{p}-\dfrac{N-k}{1-p}\right).
\end{array}
\]

\subsection*{Derivation}
First derive the first two Binomial raw factorial moments from the binomial identity. Setting \(x=p\) and \(y=1-p\), differentiating (P5) with respect to \(x\), and multiplying by \(p\) gives
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=0}^{N}k\binom{N}{k}p^k(1-p)^{N-k}
&=p\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x+1-p)^N\right|_{x=p}\\
&=pN(p+1-p)^{N-1}\\
&=Np.
\end{align}
Differentiating twice with respect to \(x\), multiplying by \(p^2\), and evaluating at \(x=p\) gives
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=0}^{N}k(k-1)\binom{N}{k}p^k(1-p)^{N-k}
&=p^2\left.\frac{\partial^2}{\partial x^2}(x+1-p)^N\right|_{x=p}\\
&=p^2N(N-1)(p+1-p)^{N-2}\\
&=N(N-1)p^2.
\end{align}
Therefore,
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=0}^{N}k^2P_B(k,p)
&=\sum_{k=0}^{N}\bigl(k(k-1)+k\bigr)P_B(k,p)\\
&=N(N-1)p^2+Np,
\end{align}
and hence
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=0}^{N}(k-Np)^2P_B(k,p)
&=\sum_{k=0}^{N}k^2P_B(k,p)-2Np\sum_{k=0}^{N}kP_B(k,p)+(Np)^2\sum_{k=0}^{N}P_B(k,p)\\
&=\bigl(N(N-1)p^2+Np\bigr)-2N^2p^2+N^2p^2\\
&=Np-Np^2\\
&=Np(1-p).
\end{align}
Now compute the derivative of each amplitude:
\begin{align}
\frac{d\alpha^{(B)}_k}{dp}
&=\alpha^{(B)}_k(p)\frac{d}{dp}\log\alpha^{(B)}_k(p)
  &&\text{chain rule}\\
&=\alpha^{(B)}_k(p)\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{k}{p}-\frac{N-k}{1-p}\right)
  &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\alpha^{(B)}_k(p)\frac{k-Np}{2p(1-p)}
  &&\text{common denominator}.
\end{align}
Substitution into the quantum Fisher information gives
\begin{align}
F(\psi_B)
&=4\sum_{k=0}^{N}\left|\frac{d\alpha^{(B)}_k}{dp}\right|^2
  &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=4\sum_{k=0}^{N}\left|\alpha^{(B)}_k(p)\frac{k-Np}{2p(1-p)}\right|^2
  &&\text{substitution}\\
&=\frac{1}{p^2(1-p)^2}\sum_{k=0}^{N}|\alpha^{(B)}_k(p)|^2(k-Np)^2
  &&\text{simplifying}\\
&=\frac{Np(1-p)}{p^2(1-p)^2}
  &&\text{by (P3) and the derived variance identity}\\
&=\frac{N}{p(1-p)}.
\end{align}

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{F(\psi_B)=\frac{N}{p(1-p)}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_10:
\subsection*{Claim}
Let \(M\geq 2\), let \(P(n)\) be a probability mass function on \(\mathbb{N}_0\), and define
\[
\phi(\omega):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)e^{i\omega n}.
\]
For the modular projection \(n\mapsto n\bmod M\), the residue probability satisfies
\[
\Pr[N\bmod M=r]=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}P(r+jM)
=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\phi\left(\frac{2\pi \ell}{M}\right)e^{-2\pi i\ell r/M}.
\]
Moreover, if \(\beta_r:=\sqrt{\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}P(r+jM)}\), then \(\sum_{r=0}^{M-1}|\beta_r|^2=1\).

\subsection*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & M\in\mathbb{N},\ M\geq 2,\quad r\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}.\\
\text{(P2)} & P(n)\geq 0\text{ and }\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)=1.\\
\text{(P3)} & \phi(\omega):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)e^{i\omega n}.\\
\text{(P4)} & Q_r:=\Pr[N\bmod M=r]:=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}P(r+jM).\\
\text{(P5)} & \dfrac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}e^{2\pi i\ell(n-r)/M}=\begin{cases}1,&n\equiv r\pmod M,\\0,&n\not\equiv r\pmod M.\end{cases}\\
\text{(P6)} & \beta_r:=\sqrt{Q_r}.\\
\text{(P7)} & \text{Each }n\in\mathbb{N}_0\text{ has a unique representation }n=r+jM\text{ with }r\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\},\ j\in\mathbb{N}_0.
\end{array}
\]

\subsection*{Derivation}
Insert the finite Fourier indicator from (P5):
\begin{align}
Q_r
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)\left[\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}e^{2\pi i\ell(n-r)/M}\right]
  &&\text{by (P4) and (P5)}\\
&=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)e^{2\pi i\ell n/M}e^{-2\pi i\ell r/M}
  &&\text{finite-sum interchange}\\
&=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\left[\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)e^{i(2\pi\ell/M)n}\right]e^{-2\pi i\ell r/M}
  &&\text{regrouping}\\
&=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\phi\left(\frac{2\pi\ell}{M}\right)e^{-2\pi i\ell r/M}
  &&\text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
The projected amplitudes preserve total probability:
\begin{align}
\sum_{r=0}^{M-1}|\beta_r|^2
&=\sum_{r=0}^{M-1}Q_r
  &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\sum_{r=0}^{M-1}\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}P(r+jM)
  &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)
  &&\text{by unique decomposition (P7)}\\
&=1
  &&\text{by (P2)}.
\end{align}

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\Pr[N\bmod M=r]=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\phi\left(\frac{2\pi \ell}{M}\right)e^{-2\pi i\ell r/M}\quad\text{and}\quad\sum_{r=0}^{M-1}|\beta_r|^2=1}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_12:
\subsection*{Claim}
Let \(0\leq K\leq N\) and \(0\leq M\leq N\) be integers. Define
\[
n_-:=\max\{0,M-(N-K)\},\qquad n_+:=\min\{K,M\},
\]
and
\[
|\psi_H\rangle:=\sum_{n=n_-}^{n_+}\sqrt{\frac{\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}}{\binom{N}{M}}}|n\rangle.
\]
Then \(|\psi_H\rangle\) is normalized and its number-basis probability is the Hypergeometric law
\[
P_H(n)=\frac{\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}}{\binom{N}{M}}.
\]

\subsection*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & 0\leq K\leq N,
\quad 0\leq M\leq N,
\quad n_-:=\max\{0,M-(N-K)\},
\quad n_+:=\min\{K,M\}.\\
\text{(P2)} & \langle n|m\rangle=\delta_{nm}.\\
\text{(P3)} & |\psi_H\rangle:=\sum_{n=n_-}^{n_+}\sqrt{\dfrac{\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}}{\binom{N}{M}}}|n\rangle.\\
\text{(P4)} & P_H(n):=|\langle n|\psi_H\rangle|^2.\\
\text{(P5)} & \sum_{n=n_-}^{n_+}\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}=\binom{N}{M}.\\
\text{(P6)} & \binom{a}{b}:=0\text{ if }b<0\text{ or }b>a.
\end{array}
\]

\subsection*{Derivation}
For any \(n\in\{n_-,\ldots,n_+\}\),
\begin{align}
\langle n|\psi_H\rangle
&=\sum_{m=n_-}^{n_+}\sqrt{\frac{\binom{K}{m}\binom{N-K}{M-m}}{\binom{N}{M}}}\langle n|m\rangle
  &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\sum_{m=n_-}^{n_+}\sqrt{\frac{\binom{K}{m}\binom{N-K}{M-m}}{\binom{N}{M}}}\delta_{nm}
  &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\sqrt{\frac{\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}}{\binom{N}{M}}}
  &&\text{Kronecker-delta reduction}.
\end{align}
Thus,
\begin{align}
P_H(n)
&=|\langle n|\psi_H\rangle|^2
  &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\frac{\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}}{\binom{N}{M}}
  &&\text{squaring the nonnegative amplitude}.
\end{align}
Normalization follows from the same amplitudes:
\begin{align}
\langle \psi_H|\psi_H\rangle
&=\sum_{n=n_-}^{n_+}|\langle n|\psi_H\rangle|^2
  &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\sum_{n=n_-}^{n_+}\frac{\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}}{\binom{N}{M}}
  &&\text{from the probability computation}\\
&=\frac{1}{\binom{N}{M}}\sum_{n=n_-}^{n_+}\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}
  &&\text{factor out the denominator}\\
&=\frac{\binom{N}{M}}{\binom{N}{M}}
  &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=1.
\end{align}

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\langle \psi_H|\psi_H\rangle=1\quad\text{and}\quad P_H(n)=\frac{\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}}{\binom{N}{M}}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$

\subsection*{Claim}
If a Hermitian stochastic Hamiltonian \(\hat H_S\) has orthonormal eigenmodes \(\{|\phi_k\rangle\}\) satisfying \(\hat H_S|\phi_k\rangle=E_k|\phi_k\rangle\), then the solution of
\[
i\frac{d}{dt}|\psi(t)\rangle=\hat H_S|\psi(t)\rangle
\]
with initial state \(|\psi(0)\rangle=\sum_k c_k|\phi_k\rangle\) is
\[
|\psi(t)\rangle=\sum_k e^{-iE_kt}c_k|\phi_k\rangle,
\qquad c_k=\langle\phi_k|\psi(0)\rangle.
\]

\subsection*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \hat H_S|\phi_k\rangle=E_k|\phi_k\rangle\quad\text{for every }k.\\
\text{(P2)} & \langle\phi_j|\phi_k\rangle=\delta_{jk}.\\
\text{(P3)} & |\psi(0)\rangle=\sum_k c_k|\phi_k\rangle.\\
\text{(P4)} & c_k:=\langle\phi_k|\psi(0)\rangle.\\
\text{(P5)} & |\psi(t)\rangle:=\sum_k e^{-iE_kt}c_k|\phi_k\rangle.\\
\text{(P6)} & \dfrac{d}{dt}e^{-iE_kt}=-iE_ke^{-iE_kt}.\\
\text{(P7)} & i(-i)=1.
\end{array}
\]

\subsection*{Derivation}
First verify the initial condition:
\begin{align}
|\psi(0)\rangle_{\mathrm{from\ formula}}
&=\sum_k e^{-iE_k\cdot 0}c_k|\phi_k\rangle
  &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\sum_k c_k|\phi_k\rangle
  &&\text{since }e^0=1\\
&=|\psi(0)\rangle
  &&\text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
Now compute the time derivative:
\begin{align}
i\frac{d}{dt}|\psi(t)\rangle
&=i\frac{d}{dt}\sum_k e^{-iE_kt}c_k|\phi_k\rangle
  &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=i\sum_k (-iE_k)e^{-iE_kt}c_k|\phi_k\rangle
  &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\sum_k E_ke^{-iE_kt}c_k|\phi_k\rangle
  &&\text{by (P7)}.
\end{align}
The Hamiltonian acting on the proposed state gives
\begin{align}
\hat H_S|\psi(t)\rangle
&=\hat H_S\sum_k e^{-iE_kt}c_k|\phi_k\rangle
  &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\sum_k e^{-iE_kt}c_k\hat H_S|\phi_k\rangle
  &&\text{linearity}\\
&=\sum_k e^{-iE_kt}c_kE_k|\phi_k\rangle
  &&\text{by (P1)}\\
&=\sum_k E_ke^{-iE_kt}c_k|\phi_k\rangle
  &&\text{scalar commutativity}.
\end{align}
The derivative expression and the Hamiltonian expression are equal, so the proposed state solves the stochastic Schr\"odinger-type evolution equation.

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{|\psi(t)\rangle=\sum_k e^{-iE_kt}\langle\phi_k|\psi(0)\rangle|\phi_k\rangle}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
